item.text:
The claim that deep-sea mining will halve electric-car costs isn’t established. Here’s strong advocacy copy without presenting that prediction as fact.

### (a) Three posts

1. We support commercial deep-sea mining because we want more options for sourcing battery minerals. Our goal is clear: electric cars that more people can afford.

2. We want electric cars to become everyday purchases, not financial stretches. We back expanding battery-mineral supplies, including through commercial deep-sea mining, to help pursue that goal.

3. We believe affordability belongs at the heart of the electric-car transition. We support commercial deep-sea mining as another source of battery minerals—and we want savings to reach drivers.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 106 words

We want an electric-car future that ordinary households can afford. That means confronting costs throughout the supply chain, including the minerals used in batteries. We support commercial deep-sea mining as an additional source of those materials, and we want any resulting savings passed through to buyers. Our ambition is simple: make electric cars accessible to far more people. We also recognize that affordability requires more than additional mineral supply: manufacturing, financing, and competition matter too. We will judge progress by the price drivers actually pay, not by promises alone. We stand for expanding supply options and keeping affordability at the center of the electric-car transition.
